## Deviations from spec (agreed)

- **S07-T1 (owner, plan 2026-11-21):** T1 is three PRs, not two: T1a (D2, the venue model, create with D13's warning
  and the check endpoint, the venue read), T1b (update, directory, lifecycle), T1c (aliases, identifiers,
  `IVenueDirectory`). `DocumentsQueryInteger` gains `maximum` and `default` in T1b, for People's list too (the S06
  carry-over). Tenancy's `TenantAccess` gains the tenant's `Country`, so a venue without a country takes the tenant's
  (D3). Q54 and Q55: the defaults.
  T1b (owner, plan 2026-11-21): two PRs, T1b-1 (update, lifecycle, status history) and T1b-2 (directory). The
  directory sorts by a new `sort_key` (the normalised name, word order kept, collation "C"). A PUT without `slug`
  keeps the venue's slug; an update is a correction allowed in every status, `ARCHIVED` included (as people's); a PUT
  without `country` takes the tenant's; the directory's `q` matches names only until T1c adds aliases and identifiers.

- **S05-T5b2a (owner, plan 2026-11-16):** D17's Settings → **Sports** is labelled **Enabled sports** (navigation entry and
  page, `/t/{slug}/settings/sports`), so it isn't confused with the workspace's **Sports** (the definitions). T5b2 is two
  PRs (T5b2a, T5b2b). D17's console **Sports** is extended to **Sports, Formats and Rules templates** under
  `platform.sport.read`, mirroring the workspace (T5b2 Q2; built in S05-T5b2b, review #93 R1).

- **S05-T5a2 (owner, plan 2026-11-15):** D14 gives `tenant.sport.read` to every tenant role; it goes to the roles

- Integration tests share one `TestApp.Clock` (`FakeTimeProvider`) for the whole run and nothing resets it (S07-T1b-1):
  a test that advances it by days moves every later test's "now" (an official's licence expired, the demo seeder's

  so neither the trigram index on `name_key` nor an index on `city_key` serves it, and it scans the tenant's venues
  (people's finder does the same). Fine at venue volumes; add `(tenant_id, city_key)` or switch to `%` with

  and teams (more rows) are planned.

- Duplicate check (S06-T2a): like the directory's search, `similarity(name_key, …) >= 0.6` can't use the trigram
  indexes, so each check filters the tenant's people, and it reads at most 200 matching rows before classifying

- Sport definitions (the next task touching `sport-definition.schema.json`, at the latest S15 with rugby): its `code`
  pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$` allows a trailing or double `_` that `ck_sport_definitions_variant`/`_sport` refuse, and
  `variant`, `sport` and `name` have no `maxLength` for their columns, so such a file passes the startup check and fails
  the seed with a raw database error. Bound it as the format schema is (review #82 R1, part left by the builder's
  default; owner may pull it forward).
- S15 (`GROUPS_THEN_KNOCKOUT`, the first multi-stage format): `FormatDefinitionRules` checks a parameter read by two
  generators only against the first one's type and values, and reports a shape problem once per stage; check against
  every generator and report once (S05-T3a pre-review).

**From S04** (each names its trigger)
- At the staff limit the screen disables **Invite someone**, so a pending address can't be invited again for a new
  link although the server allows it (a re-invitation takes no seat, D13; #73 R2). Offer it, for example a "Send a new
  link" action on a pending invitation. (Later, admin web)
- The console's renew dialog shows its first day with a client copy of `TenantSubscription.RenewalStartOn`
  (`renewalStart`, `subscription-panel.tsx`; #71 R5). Have `GET …/tenants/{tenantId}/subscription` return
  `renewalStartsOn` and drop the copy. (The next task that changes the platform subscription read)

**Identity and access** (from S03; each names its trigger)
- OpenAPI list queries (S03-T6c1): `status` and `limit` on `GET …/members`, `…/invitations` and the platform tenant
  list are typed as strings, so the generated client can't send `limit` as a number (the admin app uses the default,
  25). Document them as their enum and integer. (Any task touching those endpoints)
- An invitation's version changes when its email is sent (S03-T6c1): an admin who lists invitations and acts on one
  right away sees a concurrency conflict (revoke is sent without `If-Match`, owner #58). The same send also makes
  suspending or removing a member with pending invitations answer `AUTH_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` for a moment (their
  invitations are revoked in the same save; `ChangeMemberStatusHandler`). Decide whether sending the email should
  change the version. (Later)
- Emailed links go out before their token's hash is saved (the outbox saves the consumer's changes after the send):
  invitations (`InvitationEmailConsumer`; a link opened within moments answers `404 AUTH_INVITATION_TOKEN_INVALID`,
  #58 R1, CI) and password resets (`PasswordResetEmailConsumer`; `AUTH_RESET_TOKEN_INVALID`, #58 re-review N2). e2e
  waits for an invitation's token (`linkFromEmail` polls the lookup); a reset link has no lookup to poll, so the reset
  e2e relies on the time it takes to type two passwords (accepted risk until the fix). A person who clicks that fast
  sees "link not valid". Save before sending, or let the pages retry. (Later)
- A member who suspends or removes themselves lands on "Page not found" (`me` lists active memberships only; tested
  since S03-T6c2b). It is honest but bare: say "You no longer have access to {tenant}" instead. (Later, admin web)
- Member changes (S03-T4b1 pre-review): the audit scope counts as recorded at `SavedChanges`, before an explicit
  transaction commits; `MemberChanges` commits with `CancellationToken.None`, but a failing commit would still roll back
  unaudited. Mark the scope recorded on commit when a transaction is open (BuildingBlocks `DbTransactionInterceptor`).
  The concurrent last-owner test can pass without the lock when the two requests run one after the other; a
  deterministic test would hold the advisory lock on a test connection. (Later)
- Invitation emails are kept for ever (#49 N1): `identity.invitations.email`/`normalized_email` (`PRIVATE`) stay on
  revoked, expired and accepted invitations, for people who never joined too. With the privacy work (ADR-0015): redact
  or purge them on invitations never accepted, some time after they were revoked or expired. (Privacy tooling,
  Phase 9)
- Invitation acceptance, the double use (S03-T4c2a pre-review): `The_same_link_used_twice_at_once…` also passes when
  the two requests run one after the other (the second gets `AUTH_INVITATION_ALREADY_ACCEPTED`), so the unique-index
  catch and the `DuplicateEmail` branch of `AcceptInvitationHandler` aren't shown to run. A deterministic test would
  create the user or membership between the handler's reads and its save. (Later, with the last-owner lock test)
- Members with no tenant-wide role read no capabilities (S03-T5a, owner; #52 R1): an action without a resource is
  granted only tenant-wide, so `GET /api/admin/v1/me/capabilities` is 403 for a member whose only roles are below the
  tenant: `TEAM_MANAGER` (team only), or `COMPETITION_MANAGER`, `RESULTS_OFFICER`, `DATA_ENTRY` or `SCORER` assigned
  at one competition or contest, even with `scopeType`/`scopeId` for their own resource (the S03-T6b2 shell shows the
  403's reason). Decide how such a member reads their capabilities when requests carry resource scopes. (S08, which builds the
  `TEAM` scope chain; moved from S06 by the S05 slice review: S06 adds no resource below the tenant. S08 also gives
  `TEAM_MANAGER` `sport.read` and `tenant.sport.read` if the owner wants them (S05-T1b2, T5a2 deviations) and corrects the
  `IdentityRoles` comment and authorization.md, which still say S06)
- An invitation a member sends at the same instant as their suspension or removal can commit after it and stay pending
  (S03-T5b, Q20; owner: accepted). Close it if it matters: refuse lookup and accept when the inviter is no longer an
  active member. (Later)
- Tests that order audit entries by ID (`AuditTestData.EntriesAsync`) see entries written at one fake-clock instant
  in random order (UUIDv7 from `AuditScope`'s clock); compare such entries without order, or order by something
  stable (S03-T3, found in `PasswordResetTests`). (Any task touching audit tests)
- Audit screens (#43 N1): a successful sign-in is audited with actor `ANONYMOUS` and entity = the user, and a new
  account's invitation acceptance by `ANONYMOUS` with the user in its metadata (the slice demo e2e checks both that
  way); if the screens filter by actor, consider recording them as the user. (Audit explorer, S13)
- Logout deletes the cookie only (no server-side session store): a copied cookie lives until it expires or the
  security stamp changes. Identity's lockout uses the system clock (`UserManager` takes no `TimeProvider`). (Security
  review, Phase 9; S03-T2a)
- Password reset email: a failed send is retried by the outbox with a new token (by design), but no test makes the
  sender fail and checks the retry (S03-T2b). (Later)
- The CLI's Serilog → `LogLevel` mapping (`UseHostLogLevels`, S03-T1a) has no test; move it into the Host and unit-test it
  if the CLI's logging grows (T1a pre-review N2). The `create-platform-admin` unique-index race path has no test (two
  concurrent runs) (T1a pre-review M2). (Later)

**First deployment (infrastructure task after M1, with Q10)**
- **Before the first public deployment (S02-T5b):** the public app forwards the `Host` header it receives to `/site`;
  behind a production proxy it must read that proxy's forwarded host instead (and the API must list the app's address
  in `ForwardedHeaders`). Set `MSP_API_URL` for the public app (default `http://localhost:5080`); without it every
  public page is a 500. After `seed --category DEMO` against a running API, a demo host may stay "unknown" for up to
  60 s (host cache); `pnpm e2e` seeds before it starts the API.
- **First deployment (S03 D14):** the data protection key ring (`identity.data_protection_keys`) is stored
  unencrypted; protect it at rest (`ProtectKeysWithAzureKeyVault`) in every deployed environment.
- **First deployment (ADR-0016 infrastructure task, with Q10):** set `Platform:BaseDomain` and
  `ForwardedHeaders:KnownProxies`/`KnownNetworks` (the public web's server) in each environment. Without proxies,
  forwarding is off and every public request through the web server resolves the API's own host → 404 (S02-T3b
  pre-review). Outside Development and Testing a missing or `localhost` base domain stops the API and the CLI (#35 R1).
  Changing the base domain later needs a data step that rewrites the existing platform subdomains (or adds new
  primaries): the backfill never touches existing rows (#35 N1).
- **Blocking gate, per-IP rate limits through the admin web (#44 M2, #56 R2; owner: accepted until then).** Next.js's
  `/api/*` rewrite neither adds nor appends `X-Forwarded-For`: it passes on whatever the client sent (checked in
  S03-T6b1). Two failure modes until this is done: (a) where the API trusts the Next server as a proxy (loopback in
  Development), anyone who can reach the Next server picks their own per-IP key for login, forgot-password and
  invitation; (b) where it doesn't, every admin sign-in shares the Next server's one bucket, so the login limit
  (20 a minute) is platform-wide and one client can lock everyone else out. Before deploying: the admin web is
  reachable only through the edge; the edge overwrites or appends `X-Forwarded-For` (or the API reads
  `CF-Connecting-IP` from trusted edges only); the API lists the admin web's address in `ForwardedHeaders:KnownProxies`
  with the right `ForwardLimit`; a test proves two clients behind the full chain get separate limits.
- The API needs `ConnectionStrings:Platform` (`sp_platform`) at runtime for the audit trail (S02-T2b): provision that
  secret for the API in Key Vault with the staging setup, or every audited request fails there (#33 N1).
- SMTP provider for `IEmailSender` and `Email:From` on the real domain (S03 D13); the key ring's encryption is above.
- Media (S06): allow `pg_trgm` in Azure's `azure.extensions` server parameter before `migrate` (the Registry
  migration creates it); the Azure Blob adapter and SAS URLs (Q41); a media root or container per environment.
- Run `seed --category CONFIGURATION` in every environment after `migrate` (S04: the plans); without it no tenant has
  plan values.
- Platform staff roles (Q22): `PLATFORM_SUPPORT` can't be granted and no platform role can be revoked; the CLI
  commands come before the first deployment (S03 slice review).

**Infrastructure task after M1**
- Denials cost a permanent row each (#23 R2): rate-limit `/api/admin`, `/api/platform` and `/api/account` at the edge
  (Cloudflare), with the `/health/*` item below (infrastructure task after M1). Decided (S03 D3): anonymous denials
  keep one row each; login and forgot-password are also rate-limited in the API (done, S03-T2b: in memory, per API
  instance, so N instances allow N times the limit until the edge limits exist).
- A failed direct audit write (denial, failure, read) is only logged: the response is already written. Alert on that
  Error with the `FAILED` outbox alert below (infrastructure task after M1; S01-T6a).
- Alert on any `FAILED` outbox message (OpenTelemetry counter or gauge): with strict ordering one holds back its
  aggregate's later events until re-driven (infrastructure task after M1; #20 R3).
- `/health/ready` is anonymous and runs `SELECT 1` on every hit: expose `/health/*` only to the load balancer and
  probes, or rate-limit them at the edge (infrastructure task after M1, ADR-0016; #17 R3).
- The public reference lists (S01-T7b-2) query the database and hash the body on every request (no server cache,
  owner): rate-limit `/api/public` at the edge and let the CDN honour `Cache-Control`/`ETag` (infrastructure task
  after M1, with the `/health/*` item above).

**Owner decisions / housekeeping**
- Merge style (owner, 2026-10-18): merge commits, not squash. For stacked PRs, retarget the next PR to `main`
  before merging it.
- The prototype's old branches (`agent/*`, `codex/*`, `feature/*`, `ci/*`) are not all covered by tag
  `prototype-v0`; keep them or tag them before deleting. (The merged S00 branches and `restart/kit` were deleted
  on 2026-10-17.)
- No GitHub Pro for now (owner, 2026-10-18): `main` stays without branch protection; merge only on green CI.
- Country `PS` keeps the CLDR name (owner, 2026-10-18).

**Later** (each item names its trigger)
- Moving `BuildingBlocks/Modules` to a `BuildingBlocks.Web` project is optional, not planned (reviewer guidance on #13).
- **Branding/PRO (custom domains):** `GetSiteHandler` throws (500) if a tenant resolves through an `ACTIVE` domain but
  has no `ACTIVE` primary one. Impossible today (the platform subdomain is always primary and `ACTIVE`); once a
  platform subdomain can be `DISABLED`, keep one active primary per visible tenant or fall back to the resolved host
  (S02-T3b pre-review).
- The audit middleware's exception path (`FAILURE` with `PLATFORM_UNEXPECTED_ERROR`) has no test: no audited endpoint
  can throw yet. Add one with the first audited endpoint that can (S01-T6a).
- Audit retention and partitioning by `occurred_at` (pack spec 40 §7): with the retention job (S01-T6a).
- `platform.outbox.read` (and T6b's `platform.audit.read`) write an entry per page: diagnostics and audit screens must
  not auto-refresh by polling (#23 review).
- `GET …/diagnostics/outbox?status=…` orders by `id` and the only status index is `(status, next_attempt_at,
  sequence)`: with a large `PROCESSED` history PostgreSQL sorts or walks the primary key. Add an index on `(status, id)`
  if the page gets slow, at the latest with the retention job (S01-T5b-2 pre-review).
- Outbox and inbox tables grow forever: add a retention job for `PROCESSED` messages and old inbox rows (Hangfire,
  first slice that adds scheduled jobs; S01-T5a).
- Human-readable console logs in Development (owner, #17 re-review): a readable console formatter behind a
  setting, used by the Development launch profile; JSON stays everywhere else. Can ride the next PR.
- `ProblemDetails:TypeBaseUri` is the placeholder `https://errors.sportsplatform.invalid/` until Q10 (domain).
- Reference names are English only: CLDR has Swahili, French and other names for the same codes; add a localised
  name per language with the first non-English UI (S01-T7b-1).
- The OpenAPI document gives `time-zones?country=` no `pattern` (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) and documents no `ETag`/`Cache-Control`
  response headers on the reference lists (the endpoint descriptions say both): add them when the OpenAPI document gets
  header support (#27 R1; the first web consumer of the lists came in S03–S04 without them, S05 slice review).
- tzdata releases several times a year: rerun `build-reference-data.cs` with a new `Tzdata` pin when one changes a
  zone the customers use (the API host's own tzdata, used by `TimeZoneInfo`, comes with its container image).
- Token colour values are placeholders (`web/packages/tokens/tokens.css`); owner/Branding (S22) to confirm. The
  dark palette is written twice in that file; keep both blocks in sync.
- ESLint stays on 9.x until eslint-config-next's plugins support ESLint 10; TypeScript stays below 6.1 until
  typescript-eslint supports it.
- Colour-literal checks have known gaps and false positives (S00 Implementation notes, T2).
- pnpm 12's minimum-release-age policy is on: new package versions are installable about a day after release.
- The AR-33 test exempts the whole Host. When the first infrastructure adapter project lands (the Azure Blob adapter,
  Q41; S06's local-disk adapter needs no cloud SDK), replace the exemption with an explicit allow-list of adapter

- Dependency updates are manual (exact pins everywhere): add Dependabot or Renovate for NuGet, npm and GitHub

- Official licences are overwritten in place (S06-T4b2): a renewal replaces the grade, licence number and valid-until,
